models_evaluated: commercial AI lung nodule detection system

links.outcome: Radiologist-with-AI vs conventional reading performance, and stand-alone AI performance
links.effect: AI-assisted sensitivity 72.4% vs 32.1% conventional (p=.008); accuracy 98.5% vs 96.0%. Stand-alone AI had 381 false positives in 634 patients, but radiologists reported only one, so team performance exceeded stand-alone AI.
links.quote: The AI-assisted interpretation group compared with the conventional interpretation group showed higher sensitivity (72.4% vs 32.1%, respectively; p = .008), accuracy (98.5% vs 96.0%, p = .005), and frequency of management changes (55.2% vs 25.0%, p = .02), without significant difference in specificity (99.7% vs 98.9%, p = .11), diagnostic yield (3.2% vs 1.4%, p = .30), or false-referral rate (0.3% vs 1.1%, p = .10).

links.outcome: Radiologist acceptance of AI false-positive detections (automation bias)
links.effect: Stand-alone AI had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false positive was reported as positive by radiologists.
links.quote: Stand-alone AI correctly detected metastasis in 24 of 29 patients but had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false-positive was reported as positive by interpretating radiologists.
